target: AG1’s claim that renewables can effectively replace fossil fuels because some countries already get high shares of electricity from renewables
objection: High-renewable country examples only show that some places can generate a large share of electricity from renewables; they do not prove renewables can replace all fossil fuels, especially in transportation, industrial heat, and winter reliability at the scale of large countries.

target: AG1’s claim that alternative energy can replace fossil fuels soon
objection: The United States has never exceeded about 20% alternative energy use historically, which AG2 says undercuts the idea that renewables can effectively replace fossil fuels anytime soon.

target: AG1’s suggestion that nuclear energy should be part of the solution
objection: Nuclear should not be treated as a serious climate solution because accidents like Fukushima can erase the carbon-free gains and make nuclear an unreliable replacement strategy for global warming.

target: AG1’s argument that electrifying end uses and adding low-carbon electricity can eliminate most fossil-fuel use
objection: This still does not solve the core feasibility problem for large countries: renewables must provide firm, year-round, dispatchable power for winter peaks and industrial demand, which AG2 says remains the real bottleneck.

target: AG1’s use of Norway, Costa Rica, and Paraguay as proof of scalability
objection: Those countries are not good templates for large countries because their very high renewable electricity shares depend on special hydro/geothermal geography and established systems, not on conditions typical of large, seasonal, and geographically ordinary countries.

target: AG1’s claim that high-renewable systems plus portfolios can provide the needed firm power
objection: Relying on renewables-first or even renewables-plus-nuclear can hinder realistic change because the speed and dispatchability required to replace fossil fuels at scale are not realistically achieved that way in large countries.

target: AG1’s claim that high-renewable countries show a path to replacing fossil fuels
objection: High-renewable countries do not demonstrate that broad fossil replacement is achievable on normal terrain and under typical seasonal constraints, so they are not decisive evidence for large-country transition feasibility.

target: AG1’s claim that nuclear is a fast low-carbon option
objection: Nuclear is not a dependable global-warming solution because Fukushima-type extreme events can wipe out the carbon-free benefit, and nuclear is too slow to solve the near-term climate problem.

target: AG1’s broader portfolio approach that includes electrification, storage, transmission, and low-carbon dispatchable sources
objection: The hard parts of fossil replacement are not just resource availability but time and matching: industrial heat, cement, chemicals, transport, and winter peaks require energy qualities and dispatch timing that variable renewables plus incremental grid changes cannot meet quickly enough.

target: AG1’s claim that natural gas should be phased out rather than used as a transition fuel
objection: Natural gas is already built for dispatchable, high-capacity electricity and heat, so it is the practical bridge fuel because it can rapidly cut emissions using existing plants, pipelines, and operational flexibility while cleaner capacity scales.

target: AG1’s implication that gas is mainly a delay tactic and should not be central to the transition
objection: The realistic policy response is not to ban gas immediately but to use strict transition timelines so gas declines as clean firm capacity and electrification scale.

target: AG1’s claim that a phased substitution can quickly displace fossil fuels through electrification and renewable-derived fuels
objection: That still assumes hard fossil uses can be replaced quickly, but green hydrogen and e-fuels require large additional renewable surpluses and new industrial infrastructure, so they cannot deliver a fast system-wide replacement of fossil fuels.

target: AG1’s idea that alternative energy can effectively replace fossil fuels even if some sectors remain difficult to electrify
objection: Alternative energies can and should expand, but they do not effectively replace fossil fuels for large countries in time for most fossil demand to disappear; natural gas remains the practical bridge because it can rapidly cut emissions while renewables, storage, transmission, and electrification build out.

target: AG1’s claim that replacement does not need to be instantaneous across all sectors to be effective
objection: For large countries, renewable replacement is not effective unless it can eliminate the bulk of fossil fuels fast enough to meet the emissions timeline, and AG2 argues that the remaining hard-to-electrify sectors make that impossible without fossil bridging.

target: AG1’s claim that electrification plus clean fuels can displace fossil fuels on the needed timescale
objection: Even if electrification reduces some fossil energy demand, fossil fuels will not be eliminated until the grid can reliably meet the new loads and clean fuels for remaining sectors are ramped, which the historical slow scaling of alternative energy in the U.S. shows has not happened quickly enough.
